source_note: Hand-authored — slot progression tables and casting rules are fixed mechanics. The actual spell catalog (900+ named spells) is NOT included here; see README for why and how to fetch it.

arcane.flavor: Structured, technical magic drawn from study and theory.

divine.flavor: Magic granted by or channeled from a deity or divine force.

occult.flavor: Magic drawn from esoteric, forbidden, or mind-bending sources.

primal.flavor: Magic drawn from the raw forces of nature and the elements.

spell_ranks.cantrips: Rank-0 spells that can be cast at will (still consume the caster's normal actions) and automatically scale to half the caster's level rounded up (minimum rank 1) when cast.
spell_ranks.heightening: Many spells have a 'Heightened' entry describing an improved effect when cast using a higher-rank slot (or, for cantrips/at-will effects, at higher character level). Always cast at the rank of the slot used unless a spell says otherwise.

prepared.description: Choose spells from your full spell list (or spellbook, for Wizards) each day/via preparation and place them into your available slots. Once prepared and cast, that specific spell is expended for the day.
prepared.notes: Wizards prepare from a spellbook they must maintain; Clerics and Druids prepare from their full class spell list without needing a spellbook.

spontaneous.description: Choose a limited repertoire of known spells as you level up. Each day you gain a number of slots per rank; you may cast any known spell into any slot of its rank or higher (heightened) that you have available.
spontaneous.notes: Fewer known spells than prepared casters, but full flexibility on which spell fills which slot that day.

bounded_prepared_or_spontaneous_hybrids.description: Hybrid martial/caster classes with a smaller, level-gated spell list and slot progression than full casters, tied to their martial abilities.

focus_spells.description: Granted by certain class features, feats, or archetypes (e.g., domains, bloodline focus spells, hybrid study focus spells). Cast using Focus Points instead of spell slots.
focus_spells.focus_pool: Most characters with focus spells start with a 1-point Focus Pool, which can grow to a maximum of 3 points via certain feats/features.
focus_spells.refocus: Spend 10 minutes performing an activity related to your focus spells (e.g., prayer, meditation, practice) during downtime or exploration to regain 1 Focus Point, up to your max.

rituals.description: Powerful, usually non-combat magic that isn't tied to any one class. Rituals require no spell slot but need one or more casters meeting a proficiency rank requirement, a casting time (often hours), a cost in secondary materials/currency, and sometimes additional participants.

full_caster_slots_prepared.description: Spell slots per spell rank, per caster level, for full prepared casters (Wizard, Cleric, Druid). Rows = character level, columns = spell rank 1-10. Cantrips are unlimited and not tracked here.

full_caster_slots_spontaneous.description: Spell slots per spell rank, per caster level, for full spontaneous casters (Bard, Sorcerer, Oracle). Spontaneous casters get fewer slots at low rank than prepared casters but the same top-end progression.
full_caster_slots_spontaneous.note: Approximation of standard progression; verify against the current class chapter for the specific class, since spontaneous tables shifted slightly between classes historically. Treat as a reasonable default, not gospel — cross-check against live class data before using in a real game.

cantrip_scaling.rule: A cantrip's rank equals half your level rounded up (minimum 1), for all casting classes.

known_spellcaster_variance_warning: The exact class-by-class tables above (esp. spontaneous) should be treated as a solid working default, not verbatim from the rulebook for every class — some classes (e.g., Summoner, Magus, Witch) use bespoke bounded tables rather than the full-caster ones shown here. Cross-reference the specific class entry before hard-coding this into a production DM tool.
